rules.alternatives: No general CE hours: APRN renewal requires current national certification in the role and population focus. An APRN recognized in Wyoming before January 1, 1999 with continuous licensure but no national certification shows instead 40 CE hours in the role and population focus plus 400 hours of APRN practice in the last 2 years. The 3 controlled-substance hours apply to every APRN in both cases.

topics.who: Every APRN at renewal (WSBN Rules Ch. 2, Sec. 14(c)(i)(C)): responsible prescribing of controlled substances or treatment of substance use disorders; certificate uploaded with the renewal application

rules.notes: All nursing licenses renew biennially in even years; the 2026 renewal window is Oct 1 to Dec 31. Fees: $180 for the first national certification, $70 per additional certification, $70 for prescriptive authority. The Board's renewal page lists the 3 controlled-substance hours next to prescriptive authority, but the rule (Section 14(c)(i)(C)) requires them of every APRN.
rules.legal_basis: W.S. §33-21-129 (Nurse Practice Act); WSBN Rules Chapter 2, Section 14
rules.rule_quote: (c) APRN. (i) An APRN shall demonstrate continuing competency by submitting evidence of: (A) Current national certification as an APRN in the recognized role and population focus area; or (B) If recognized as an APRN in the State prior to January 1, 1999, and has maintained continuous licensure, but is not nationally certified, the APRN shall submit evidence of: (I) Forty (40) hours of continuing education related to the APRN's recognized role and population focus area; and (II) Four hundred (400) hours of active nursing practice as an APRN during the last two (2) years. (C) An APRN shall also submit evidence of three (3) hours of continuing education related to the responsible prescribing of controlled substances or treatment of substance abuse disorders.
